verdicts.trueWording: I try not to leave a clue more than once
verdicts.note: Raw PDF (gwern.net, 31pp, pdftotext -layout); chapter 9, Jordan interview, Soldier-of-Arete clues exchange. Wolfe's answer opens with this sentence; he adds that repeated clues bother him in other writers' books.

verdicts.trueWording: you are writing for somebody that is a lot dumber
verdicts.note: Same answer, one sentence later: the left-handed-hero example, 'if you tell me five times', then this clause closing 'than I am'. Both limbs (five times; dumber than he is) on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: leave all the clues that I think the reader
verdicts.note: Same answer; the sentence continues 'is going to require, sometimes more than they require', supplying the 'sometimes more' limb.

verdicts.trueWording: the great majority of it consists of finding more clues
verdicts.note: Same answer, closing movement: Wolfe turns from the reader solving his books to 'a real life situation' and 'actual police work', where reasoning from clues is little of the work. The likening is his own, carried by that continuous answer rather than by an explicit 'reading is like police work' sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: Life seen superficially has very little pattern to it
verdicts.note: Later exchange on whether he writes the modern everything-is-perspective novel; he answers that the confusion can be got through, then this sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: to write about that pagan world as the pagans themselves
verdicts.note: Soldier of the Mist / Soldier of Arete exchange; the sentence ends 'wrote about it', preceded by his statement that the gods of paganism were real.

verdicts.trueWording: we are reading a very rationalistic viewpoint
verdicts.note: Immediately after 1103: 'If we read modern historians' precedes the quoted clause, which ends 'of this' - 'this' being the pagan religious world just described (temples, sacrifices to Ares or Apollo).

verdicts.trueWording: I have made use of the memory palace
verdicts.note: Frances Yates / Art of Memory exchange; the sentence ends 'system in the Soldier books, of course', after he traces the concept to Simonides.

verdicts.trueWording: a ceremony that I described in detail exactly as it was
verdicts.note: Sparta/Helots answer: the freed Helots are each given a young Spartan companion who kills him at a signal; Wolfe adds that it really took place. Both limbs on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: No, but some of them are typos
verdicts.note: Answer to Jordan's 'You didn't make up any words?'; Wolfe's 'No' takes the negative question, then the typos exception, then 'Ushas is not one of them though'.

verdicts.trueWording: a place that I could steal ideas and names from
verdicts.note: Same Ushas answer, after 'Read Qabbalic literature' and his saying he does not believe in it; 'To me it was' precedes the quoted clause.

verdicts.trueWording: reacting against an idealization of the ancient world that many people
verdicts.note: Latro's-world exchange near the Soldier of Sidon passage; the sentence ends 'have', and is followed by the anecdote of the ideal society run on slaves. Graded SUBSTANCE, not VERBATIM: the supplied quote 'reacting against an ideali-' is a pdftotext line-break artifact, not a word of the printed text.

verdicts.trueWording: enough clues were provided for such major mysteries to be solved
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture (id_ form) fetched, 200, HTML stripped locally; byline 'by Michael Andre-Driussi', April 2009, Criticism section. The sentence ends 'in the original tetrology' (the page's spelling) and is introduced by 'With the mysteries laid bare, it becomes apparent that'.

verdicts.trueWording: probably not even recognized as a mystery by most readers
verdicts.note: Same essay, paragraph before the deluge discussion: 'Urth also delivers an unambiguous answer to a major mystery that was' precedes the quoted clause, which is followed by the dash and 'the relation of New Sun and the deluge'.

verdicts.trueWording: In at least seven points in TBOTNS, Severian has intimations
verdicts.note: Next sentence of the same paragraph; it continues 'of deluge' (the page has no article) and names the howdah-ride vision as the emblematic case.
